item.title: Rust's Type Checker Implementation Is Unsound: An Empirical Study on Soundness Bugs in rustc
item.content: We systematically study 87 soundness bugs in rustc's type checker, classify their root causes across trait resolution, lifetime inference and variance, and show that a majority remain reachable from safe code. We release reproductions for each.

notes: NEGATIVE TEST for the off-domain-paper rule. Measured live: judge 0.80 / confidence 0.92 against a pipeline score of 0.32 - here the judge is RIGHT and the pipeline undervalued it. A v6 that rejects academic papers wholesale must fail on this one.

description: Paper directly about dependency-upgrade breakage detection

item.title: Update from Hell: Can Coding Agents Survive Hidden Breakage in Dependency Upgrades?
item.content: We construct a benchmark of 240 real dependency upgrades containing silent behavioural breakage and measure whether coding agents detect it. Agents catch compile-time breaks reliably but miss 71% of semantic regressions that pass the type checker.

notes: NEGATIVE TEST. Measured live: judge 0.72 / confidence 0.85, pipeline 0.308 and excluded. Directly applicable to a developer maintaining dependency-upgrade tooling.

description: Deep dive into React internals, not a beginner tutorial

item.title: How Does useEffect Actually Work?
item.content: We walk through React's fiber commit phase to show exactly when effects are scheduled, why the cleanup runs before the next effect rather than after unmount, and how the dependency array is compared with Object.is at the hook slot level.

notes: NEGATIVE TEST for the beginner rule. Measured live: judge 0.85 / confidence 0.92, pipeline 0.32 and excluded. Same technology as the beginner React question above; the difference is depth, which is exactly the discrimination being tested.

description: Tooling for a problem the user is actively hitting

item.title: Tollgate: Open-Source Hard Limits for LLM Spend
item.content: Tollgate sits in front of your LLM provider and enforces hard per-day and per-feature spend ceilings, with preflight cost estimation so the call that would cross the limit is refused rather than billed. Supports Anthropic and OpenAI.

notes: NEGATIVE TEST. Measured live: judge 0.72 / confidence 0.85, pipeline 0.278 and excluded. This app enforces exactly this mechanism and hit its own daily cap on 2026-09-01 - a case where the judge's recall beat the pipeline's.
